findings.title: Unconditional Exception Fallback in Supervisor Tool Execution Catch Block
findings.impact: Any exception raised during research delegation (such as network glitches, timeouts, or transient API errors) is unconditionally caught and immediately terminates the research phase, returning incomplete or missing notes instead of allowing retries or proper error handling.
findings.preconditions: An exception occurs during `asyncio.gather(*research_tasks)` in the `supervisor_tools` node.
findings.explanation: Line 334 evaluates `if is_token_limit_exceeded(e, configurable.research_model) or True:`, which always evaluates to `True`. As a result, all exceptions encountered during parallel research execution trigger an immediate exit to `END` rather than handling token limits specifically or bubbling up transient errors.
findings.suggestion: Remove the `or True` clause from the exception check so that non-token-limit exceptions can be appropriately handled or retried.

assessment: All six Gemini3.8 attempts failed HTTP503. No stronger-model correctness or verifier verdict was available. Preserve incomplete findings and do not publish. Subsequent comparison selects allowlisted free Gemini3.6 explicitly, without an automatic paid fallback.
diagnostic_caveat: At this revision the adapter also mapped network/timeouts to status503. The failure proves requests did not complete, not that every response was a genuine serverHTTP503. New code distinguishes transport errors.
